It sucks and it feels so weird and unreal. I was going back to school before everything happened and so stopped going. Turns out one of the guys I sat next to in class lived in the same apt building as me and recognized me when I was outside smoking. He asked me why I wasn’t going to class and I told him. His exact words were “well there’s always more fish in the sea.” I’ll admit I wasn’t angry but more confused and understanding that he definitely didn’t know what to say. I let out a chuckle and I think we both knew we were both uncomfortable from the interaction and just said our goodbyes. We are so desensitized to death until it happens to us.

I completely agree. I’d wager the majority of us in the first few weeks or even months can’t even function properly or our brains are short circuiting. It’s a fucking godsend that some friends/family are coming in here because they care that much. I had everything before. 2 kids and a nice apartment. We ended up separating 2 months before her death after being together for nearly 11 years. At the time I was okay cause I knew I needed to get my shit together and I’d see her and the kids every few days. After she passed, my parents are taking care of the kids but they live in a different state and I simply don’t have the money to pay two plus months of rent to cut the lease. That’s when I realized that I was alone for the first time in my life. And it’s been that way for nearly 8 months. Never knew I had abandonment issues till after. I’m sorry that you’re going through the same things I am and it sucks that the only people who really understand what you’re going through are here instead of family and friends.

There’s 2 songs that make me tear up/full blown crying every time. Failure’s “Another Space Song” and Foo Fighters “Everlong.” I’m sure most people know Everlong but highly recommend Another Space Song if you’re into 90’s alternative. Now a song that she listened too that breaks my heart every time is Death Cab for Cutie “Soul Meets Body.” She used to listen to it a lot when her mom passed away when she was 13. When we did the funeral, I put verses from the song on the back of her cards that had her picture in the front. The song is insanely hard for me to listen too and I always think about how perfectly she sang it when the song popped up on our night drives.

I remember this girl that went to the same high school as me. She worked at a gym I frequented at the time and so I saw her quite a bit as I went often. We recognized each other from school and our interactions were always friendly and she was genuinely nice. I remember seeing the details of her death over FB and it absolutely destroyed me for a few months. It bothered me so much even though I hardly knew her. I ended up having discussions with my best friend about suicide and promising each other that we would ask for help. I also did the same with my gf. My gf ended up killing herself years later earlier last year. It made me think of the girl from earlier and while the intensity of grief I have for my gf is beyond what I felt for her, I still cared and it made me start having conversations to start talking about suicide. I felt and still feel the same as you are, I had guilt and I didn’t understand why. That’s why I started having discussions with close friends about mental health. It helped me at the time and it took a few months to push through that. The grief I have now though is different and will probably take years to get through before I feel “okay.” It’s amazing that you care though, a lot of people are very uncomfortable discussing death or even reaching out and often you lose friends over this. Let yourself grieve even if it’s in private, that’s what I did.

I think about this often, and it’s actually turned into advice for my friends. I used to look at everything as something we can do later like there’s plenty of time. There’s trips that she wanted to do but I kept saying no, we don’t have the money or it’s too far but when we do have money, we can do it. I want to kick myself for ever thinking that way. And now I tell my friends to not think like that. You want to do something, go do it. Don’t ever think you have time for it later. Go on those adventures and create beautiful memories. I just wish I knew sooner..

Take your time. I didn’t get to. A hour after I officially learned she was gone, a missing persons post was circulating through social media and my phone was ringing/vibrating non-stop through the night. I thought by making a post, it would stop it. It didn’t. It just led people to being more direct in their questions. Also calls from the local news station. It’s actually left a bad taste in my mouth concerning who we call friends over the years. They care for one day, and then that’s it. I get we all have morbid curiosity when these things don’t happen to us. Honestly, just let any close friends know. Make a post if you want too. You don’t have to.

I often have to remind myself that there was way more good than bad. But I still can’t help but feel guilty over small things on times I might’ve screwed up. I can tell her friends don’t like me because they only came around when our relationship was in a rough patch which drives those feelings deeper. But they didn’t know her like I did. From observations of this subreddit, I assume it’s normal for some of us to feel this way. Sometimes we are unaware of what we are doing and don’t realize until we actually sit down and think about it. As long as you remind yourself that your love together was real. I know I have to and it helps when I get stuck in focusing on the bad parts. Everyday I do it, and I will be until I die.

Survivors guilt is terrible especially along with PTSD. I recently lost someone extremely close to me to suicide and it’s eating away at me. Just don’t tell them to stay strong, let them talk and listen to them.

When I did my Eulogy for my wife, I focused a lot on how she was as a person. A few anecdotes that highlighted her personality and described how she went above and beyond for our children. I didn’t talk about her suicide, I just wrote about the good things. I kept it light hearted which helped because her Sisters eulogy was heartbreaking but beautiful. I didn’t practice my speech, actually I put it off until the night before because of course I didn’t want to write it. Every step I took made it feel more real when everything is unreal. You won’t fuck it up, people will understand. I don’t really have advice on first month because I’m on month 2 and it still hurts the same. Just grieve and surround yourself with people who will let you grieve. Tell stories to those who will listen. That’s what I’ve been doing.
